THIS CCC IS FILED UNDER SECTIONS 11 AND 12 OF THE CONTEMPT OF COURTS ACT, PRAYING TO INITIATE CONTEMPT PROCEEDINGS AGAINST THE ACCUSED FOR NON- COMPLIANCE OF HIGH COURT ORDER DATED 11-10-2023 IN WP NO.202849/2023 VIDE ANNEXURE-A AND ISSUE ANY OTHER DIRECTIONS AS THIS HON'BLE COURT DEEMS FIT UNDER FACTS AND CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE.
THIS CCC
COMING ON FOR ORDERS THIS DAY

,
B.M.SHYAM PRASAD J., MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
The complainant alleges that the first respondent has issued Endorsement dated 01.12.2023 in deliberate disobedience of the directions of the Writ Court in W.P.No.202849/2023.

Sri Liyaqat Fareed Ustad, the learned counsel for the complainant, submits that in terms of decree dated 01.03.2019 in O.S.No.288/2018 and the directions of the Writ Court in W.P.No.202849/2023,
which is disposed of on 11.10.2023, the first respondent ought to have disbursed the total compensation of Rs.77,50,868/- amongst different claimants [including the complainant] without insisting upon all the parties to the suit to come together to make a NC: 2024:KHC-K:397-DB claim for compensation.

Sri Liyaqat Fareed Ustad further submits that the complainant, in terms of the decree dated 01.03.2019, will be entitled to a sum of Rs.7,00,000/- while the other parties to the proceedings are entitled for different sums.

It would suffice for this Court to observe that the complainant has not mentioned the details of the terms of the compromise in the representation filed with the first respondent after the writ Court's order dated 11.10.2023, nor has he produced a copy of the decree in the present proceedings, and therefore, the complainant must first file a detailed representation enclosing a decree with the first respondent and if there is any failure despite that, the complainant can approach this Court.
It only then this Court could consider whether there is reason to initiate proceedings for contempt.
